narrativeReportMd:
# Range R4→R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
No hard R4-to-R6 instance-breaking change was found for the local `Range` datatype shape. `Range.low` and `Range.high` remain optional `SimpleQuantity`-profiled `Quantity` elements with the same cardinalities, flags, and summary status.

## Scope
The analysis focused on the R4 and R6 core `StructureDefinition/Range` artifacts and supporting package metadata. Base-class changes through `Element`/`DataType` and dependency changes in `Quantity`/`SimpleQuantity` are called out as follow-up dependencies, not local `Range` findings.

## Main migration themes
The only material local change is the `rng-2` invariant expression. R6 keeps the same human rule that, when both bounds are present, low should not exceed high, but the computable expression now checks `low.value`/`high.value`, uses precision-aware boundary functions, and explicitly permits non-comparable boundaries.

## Highest-impact findings
The invariant change is mainly a validation and round-trip concern: some R6-valid ranges may not pass older R4-era validators or custom FHIRPath/XPath logic, especially where quantities are missing numeric values, have incomparable units, or rely on decimal precision boundaries.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is recommended for systems that use `Range` to enforce clinical or business thresholds, because the practical effect depends on FHIRPath engine behavior for Quantity comparison, precision boundary functions, and incomparable units.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The R6 expression appears to be a reasonable clarification and weakening rather than a hard break. A less disruptive alternative would have been to retain the R4 expression and add a separate warning or narrative clarification, but that would not provide the same computable precision-aware behavior.

## Follow-up analysis
Review the separate `DataType`, `Element`, `Quantity`, and `SimpleQuantity` reports before treating `Range` migration as complete, because inherited and referenced datatype changes can still affect generated classes and validation behavior.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: No hard local `Range` R4-to-R6 instance break was found. The main migration concern is the changed `rng-2` invariant, which can change validation results and R6-to-R4 round-tripping for boundary edge cases. Confidence is high for the computable diff and medium-high for real-world impact without rendered spec notes or validator behavior testing.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Most `Range` instances with ordinary comparable low/high quantities should migrate without structural transformation. Migration and validation test suites should focus on the ordering invariant: missing `low.value` or `high.value`, quantities with different or non-comparable units, and decimal precision cases where boundary-aware comparison differs from direct value comparison.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high that the element inventory, cardinalities, types, bindings, modifier flags, and summary flags are unchanged locally, because both StructureDefinitions were present and directly compared. Confidence in operational impact is slightly lower because the supplied inputs did not include official diff notes, rendered narrative pages, or empirical runs against R4 and R6 validators.

findings.title: Range ordering invariant now uses value presence, precision boundaries, and comparability

oldState.summary: R4 `rng-2` used a direct Quantity comparison when both `low` and `high` elements were present.

constraints.human: If present, low SHALL have a lower value than high

semanticText.short: Set of values bounded by low and high
semanticText.definition: A set of ordered Quantities defined by a low and high limit.
semanticText.comment: The stated low and high value are assumed to have arbitrarily high precision when it comes to determining which values are in the range. I.e. 1.99 is not in the range 2 -> 3.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 enforced `rng-2` with `low.empty() or high.empty() or (low <= high)`. The XPath form compared the numeric `value` children directly and did not express unit comparability or precision-boundary behavior.

newState.summary: R6 `rng-2` checks numeric value presence, skips the ordering test when boundaries are not comparable, and compares low/high precision boundaries.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The same invariant key `rng-2` appears on the same root element `Range` with the same severity and human text, so this is a changed constraint rather than a removed/replaced element.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is not a hard R4-to-R6 structural break: ordinary R4 instances with absent bounds or comparable `low <= high` values should still validate. The risk is that R6 accepts or evaluates some edge cases differently from R4, and R6 validators must support `lowBoundary()`, `highBoundary()`, and `comparable()`. R6-valid instances that depend on missing numeric values, incomparable units, or precision-boundary overlap may not be accepted by R4-era validators or transforms.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The affected cases are likely uncommon, but `Range` is often used for clinically meaningful thresholds. A system that treats an accepted range as clinically ordered without considering unit comparability or precision could make different inclusion/exclusion decisions at threshold boundaries.

justification.inferredGoal: Clarify the ordering invariant so it is precision-aware and avoids failing when one bound lacks a value or the two Quantity boundaries are not comparable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No R4-to-R6 less-breaking base-design alternative is needed because the R6 invariant preserves the Range shape and appears to broaden or clarify validation rather than invalidate R4-valid instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal is reasonable: R6 makes the existing ordering invariant explicit about value presence, Quantity comparability, and precision-aware boundaries while leaving `Range.low` and `Range.high` cardinalities and types unchanged. On the available StructureDefinition evidence this is not a hard R4-to-R6 base-design break; the main cost is validator/runtime behavior for edge cases and reverse-version compatibility. Because no official rationale or validator comparison was available locally, `Probably justified` is more appropriate than an unqualified `Justified`.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: This is not a backward-compatible-alternative case in the primary R4-to-R6 direction because the R6 base design already preserves the R4 structural content model and is not expected to reject ordinary R4-valid ranges. Retaining the R4 expression as the normative error rule, or adding the R6 expression only as a warning, would mainly preserve legacy validator behavior; it would not better preserve R4 instances and would fail the R6 goal of making range ordering precision- and comparability-aware. R6-to-R4 conversion rules or old-validator shims are useful mitigations, but they are not less-breaking base R6 designs.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Keeping the R4 direct comparison would improve old-validator behavioral continuity but would preserve less precise handling of missing values, Quantity comparability, and precision boundaries.

R6 `rng-2` expression checks value presence, comparability, and precision boundaries.

examples.examplesMd: The example is intentionally a boundary/precision edge case, not a complete resource. Under a precision-boundary interpretation, `2.1` as a one-decimal value can have a lower boundary that overlaps the upper boundary of `2.0`, while a direct numeric comparison would treat `2.1 <= 2.0` as false. Validator behavior should be tested in the specific FHIRPath engine used.

findings.narrativeMd: `Range.rng-2` changed from a direct comparison of `low` and `high` to a more nuanced expression that first checks whether numeric values exist, then skips the ordering check when the precision-adjusted Quantity boundaries are not comparable, and finally compares `lowBoundary()` to `highBoundary()`. This matters most to validators, custom FHIRPath engines, and cross-version transforms, not to the JSON/XML shape of `Range` instances.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid instance is not expected to become invalid in R6 solely because of this local change. The reverse direction is riskier: an R6 instance can be accepted because one bound lacks `value`, because two boundaries are not comparable, or because precision-boundary comparison succeeds even where a direct value comparison would fail. Older validators that rely on the R4 FHIRPath or XPath expression may reject such instances, and R6 validators need FHIRPath support for the boundary and comparability functions.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Keep the `low`/`high` structure unchanged, but update validation test cases and any hand-coded Range ordering logic. Include tests for absent `low.value` or `high.value`, non-comparable UCUM units, equal values with different decimal precision, and near-overlap cases such as `2.1` to `2.0`. For R6-to-R4 export, consider normalizing or flagging ranges whose validity depends on the R6-specific expression; some cases may need manual review rather than a lossless transform.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change is mostly backward-compatible for R4-to-R6 data because it does not narrow the local content model. It could have been made less behavior-changing by preserving the R4 expression and adding a new warning-level invariant for the precision-aware logic, but that would retain known ambiguity around Quantity comparability and precision.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Review impact with the actual validators in use. FHIRPath comparison behavior for Quantity, empty results, and the exact semantics of `lowBoundary()`/`highBoundary()` can determine whether a particular instance is accepted or rejected.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The R6 package contains `StructureDefinition-Range.json` with the same canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, derivation, status, and `abstract=false`. The baseDefinition shift is noted out of scope as an infrastructure/base-artifact change.
The local differential still contains only `Range`, `Range.low`, and `Range.high`; no local Range elements were added, removed, renamed, moved, split, or merged.
`Range.low` and `Range.high` remain `0..1`; the root remains `0..*` in the StructureDefinition.
Both local bound elements remain `Quantity` constrained by the `http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/SimpleQuantity` profile.
`Range` has no local Reference-typed elements or target profiles.
`Range.low` and `Range.high` have no local terminology binding. Terminology on nested Quantity fields is a dependency concern, not a local Range binding.
No fixed value, pattern value, or default value was found on local Range elements in either version.
No minValue, maxValue, maxLength, or regex value limits were found on local Range elements. The material value rule is represented as the changed `rng-2` invariant.
`Range`, `Range.low`, and `Range.high` remain non-modifier elements in the snapshot.
`Range.low` and `Range.high` remain `isSummary=true`; inherited `id` and `extension` summary flags are unchanged for the Range snapshot.
No slicing appears on local Range elements in either version.
The local short, definition, and comment text for `Range`, `Range.low`, and `Range.high` are unchanged. The semantics change found is in the computable invariant expression, not the narrative text.

No JSON/XML element names or choice-type serialization changed for local `Range` content. The local `rng-2` XPath expression present in R4 is absent in R6, which matters for XPath-based validation tooling and is covered in the constraint finding.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Low and high now explicitly declare participation in the `rng-2` condition
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The added `condition: ["rng-2"]` metadata on `Range.low` and `Range.high` does not change cardinality, type, names, or direct instance representation. It is metadata tying the elements to the root invariant.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Tools that display element-level warnings or generate validation documentation may now surface the Range ordering rule on both bound elements rather than only at the root.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: RIM mapping text was compacted
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The R6 snapshot combines the R4 root RIM mapping information into a single mapping string; this is descriptive mapping metadata and does not affect instance validation.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Mapping-documentation generators may see a textual diff, but no Range element or conformance rule depends on this mapping string.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: R6 `Range` derives from `DataType` instead of directly from `Element`. This can affect generated class hierarchies and shared datatype behavior, but it is a base/infrastructure issue that should be handled in the `DataType` and `Element` reports rather than duplicated as a local `Range` finding.

`Range.low` and `Range.high` continue to reference `SimpleQuantity`. Any breaking changes in `SimpleQuantity` or its base `Quantity` can affect valid Range bounds even though the local Range type reference did not change.
